facets.short: Measuring whether a change is real
facets.text: Statistics of evaluation and experiments: is a difference real or noise? Paired comparisons, significance testing, confidence intervals, bootstrap, A/B testing, p-hacking, multiple comparisons, variance reduction, reproducibility crisis, benchmarks and how measurements mislead.

Where large language models go wrong: hallucination, prompt sensitivity, LLM-as-a-judge bias, sycophancy, unreliable reasoning, evaluating AI capabilities honestly, skepticism about AI hype and benchmarks.

How transformers and large language models work inside: attention, tokenization, training neural networks from scratch, backpropagation, quantization and low-bit inference, long context, running models locally, GPUs and inference efficiency.
Information retrieval and search engines: how search works, inverted indexes, BM25 and ranking, embeddings and vector databases, semantic search, retrieval-augmented generation, recommender systems.
AI agents and tool use: coding agents, LLMs calling tools and APIs, multi-agent debate, memory for agents, building with Claude and LLM APIs, the future of programming with AI.
Machine learning engineering in production: data pipelines, MLOps, data quality, forecasting, model monitoring, Docker, workflow orchestration, data engineering, practical machine learning systems.
Bayesian statistics and probabilistic machine learning: Gaussian processes, uncertainty, probabilistic programming, Bayesian inference, statistical thinking, probability.
How science and research work: reading papers, citations, peer review, the scientific method, writing and communicating research, how to do great research, history of ideas in computer science.
Real-time computer graphics and rendering: shaders, WebGL, three.js, procedural generation, lighting, game engine programming, performance and draw calls, physics simulation for games.
Game design and indie game development: game feel, level design, art direction, atmospheric games like Limbo and Ori, making a game alone, why games are fun, racing games, platformers.
Cities and civic data: public transit, urbanism, city government, Boston, open data, how local politics and councils work, infrastructure, journalism with data.
Technology and attention: the attention economy, social media and doomscrolling, ad-free software, privacy and tracking, humane tech design, smartphones and wellbeing, courage and habits.
Developer tools and the craft of programming: Git internals, the command line and terminal, writing good software, simple design, debugging, open source tools, programming talks.
Visual and interface design: typography, UI design, web design, data visualization, making software beautiful and restrained, design thinking.
